claims.quote: A company applying for authority to write surety bonds in favor of the United States must be engaged in the business of writing surety or fidelity contracts at the time of its application to Treasury, whether or not also making contracts in other classes of insurance, but shall not be engaged in any type or class of business not authorized by its charter or the laws of the state in which the company is incorporated. It must be the intention of the company to engage actively in the execution of surety bonds or fidelity contracts in favor of the United States.
claims.affected_party: company applying for authority to write surety bonds in favor of the United States
claims.summary: The company must be engaged in the business of writing surety or fidelity contracts at the time of its application to Treasury, not engaged in any type or class of business not authorized by its charter or the laws of the state in which the company is incorporated, and must intend to engage actively in the execution of surety bonds or fidelity contracts in favor of the United States.

claims.quote: A company is not eligible for a certificate of authority if it only insures or reinsures risks of its parent, affiliated, or controlled unaffiliated business, or is deemed by Treasury to be primarily engaged in self-insurance.
claims.summary: A company is not eligible for a certificate of authority if it only insures or reinsures risks of its parent, affiliated, or controlled unaffiliated business, or is deemed by Treasury to be primarily engaged in self-insurance.

claims.quote: Every company not currently holding a certificate of authority wishing to apply for a certificate of authority shall submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location, and in the manner, specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surey-bonds/.
claims.affected_party: company not currently holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: Every company not currently holding a certificate of authority wishing to apply for a certificate of authority shall submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location and in the manner specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/.

claims.quote: The company shall file the following data with Treasury, and shall transmit therewith the fee in accordance with the provisions of

claims.quote: This request must indicate: (i) Whether the company has previously applied for a certificate of authority from Treasury and, if so, the date and disposition of the previous application; and (ii) Whether Treasury has ever previously issued the company a certificate of authority, the reason for termination of its certificate of authority, and the applicable dates;
claims.summary: The company must indicate whether it has previously applied for a certificate of authority from Treasury, including the date and disposition of the previous application, and whether Treasury has ever previously issued the company a certificate of authority, including the reason for termination and applicable dates.

claims.quote: The company is authorized to transact surety business; and (ii) If granted a certificate of authority, there are no restrictions upon the company preventing it from being able to execute and guarantee bonds and undertakings in judicial proceedings, and guarantee contracts to which the United States is a party;
claims.summary: The company must certify that it is authorized to transact surety business and that there are no restrictions preventing it from executing and guaranteeing bonds and undertakings in judicial proceedings and guaranteeing contracts to which the United States is a party.

claims.quote: A listing of the names of the company's current officers and directors as of the date of application, including a biographical affidavit of each officer and director per instructions online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/ ;
claims.summary: The company must provide a listing of the names of its current officers and directors as of the date of application, including a biographical affidavit of each officer and director.

claims.quote: A memorandum setting forth: (i) A comprehensive statement of the company's method of operation, including, but not limited to, underwriting guidelines, claims adjustment procedures, reinsurance philosophy, control over collateral, and significant changes in operations or corporate structure that impact its financial statements; (ii) The classes of business in which it engages; (iii) Any special underwriting agreements, management agreements, or pooling agreements in force. Copies of such agreements must be included with the memorandum;
claims.summary: The company must provide a memorandum setting forth its method of operation, classes of business, and any special underwriting, management, or pooling agreements, including copies of such agreements.

claims.quote: A certified copy of a license from its state of incorporation and a completed Surety License Form (Form No. FS 2208);
claims.summary: The company must provide a certified copy of its license from its state of incorporation and a completed Surety License Form (Form No. FS 2208).

claims.quote: A copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department including a copy of company responses to any significant findings or recommendations;
claims.summary: The company must provide a copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department, including responses to any significant findings or recommendations.

claims.quote: The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) annual statement form with all Schedules and Exhibits completed, including copies of the NAIC File Upload, showing the last two full calendar years of the company's financial condition, including proof that the company has paid-up capital of at least $250,000 in cash or its equivalent, in the case of a stock insurance company, or has net assets of not less than $500,000 over and above all liabilities, in the case of a mutual insurance company. The annual financial statement's Jurat Page (only) is to be signed (facsimile or electronic signatures are acceptable) by the company President, Secretary, and a Notary Public who shall also affix a notary seal;
claims.summary: The company must provide the NAIC annual statement form with all Schedules and Exhibits completed, including copies of the NAIC File Upload, showing the last two full calendar years of its financial condition, including proof of paid-up capital or net assets, and the Jurat Page must be signed by the company President, Secretary, and a Notary Public.

claims.quote: The Insurance Regulatory Information System (IRIS) ratio results, and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC for the last two full calendar years preceding the date of application;
claims.summary: The company must provide the Insurance Regulatory Information System (IRIS) ratio results and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC for the last two full calendar years preceding the date of application.

claims.quote: A written statement signed by the Insurance Commissioner or other proper financial officer of any state attesting that the company maintains on deposit legal investments having a current market value of not less than $100,000 for the protection of claimants, including all of its policyholders in the U.S.;
claims.summary: The company must provide a written statement signed by the Insurance Commissioner or other proper financial officer of any state attesting that it maintains on deposit legal investments with a current market value of not less than $100,000 for the protection of claimants, including all of its policyholders in the U.S.

claims.quote: (12) Copies of all reinsurance treaties currently in force along with a completed Summary of Reinsurance Treaties, per instructions provided online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/ ;
claims.summary: The company must submit copies of all reinsurance treaties currently in force along with a completed Summary of Reinsurance Treaties.

claims.summary: The company must submit a completed Schedule of Excess Risks form (Form No. FS 285-A) as of the date of the application.

claims.summary: The company must submit a Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the last two full calendar years preceding the date of application provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC.

claims.quote: (15) Such other evidence as Treasury may, in its discretion, request to establish that the company is solvent, willing, and able to meet the continuing obligation to carry out its contracts.
claims.summary: The company must submit such other evidence as Treasury may, in its discretion, request to establish that the company is solvent, willing, and able to meet the continuing obligation to carry out its contracts.

claims.quote: (2) A completed Surety License Form (Form No. FS 2208) and a certified copy of the licenses from any states indicated on the Surety License Form that were not indicated on the company's most recent form;
claims.summary: The company must submit a completed Surety License Form (Form No. FS 2208) and a certified copy of the licenses from any states indicated on the Surety License Form that were not indicated on the company's most recent form.

claims.quote: (3) A copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department including a copy of company responses to any significant findings or recommendations;
claims.summary: The company must submit a copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department including a copy of company responses to any significant findings or recommendations.

claims.quote: (5) IRIS ratio results, and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC, as of the close of the preceding year;
claims.summary: The company must submit IRIS ratio results, and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC, as of the close of the preceding year.

claims.quote: (6) A completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in
claims.summary: The company must submit a completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in.

claims.quote: A completed Schedule of Excess Risks form (Form No. FS 285-A) as of the close of the preceding quarter; (8) A Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the preceding year provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC; (9) A listing of the names of the company's current officers and directors as of the close of the preceding year, including a biographical affidavit of any new officer and director for whom a biographical affidavit was not previously provided, per instructions online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/ ; (10) A Report of Federal Business Written and/or Outstanding as of the close of the preceding year, per instructions provided online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/ ; and (11) Such other evidence as Treasury may request to establish that the company is solvent, willing, and able to meet the continuing obligation to carry out its contracts. Additionally, Treasury will publish supplemental guidance annually regarding evidence it may require, submission methods, and format of the data listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (10) of this section. claims.summary: The company must submit various forms and reports, including the Schedule of Excess Risks form, Statement of Actuarial Opinion, listing of officers and directors, Report of Federal Business, and any other evidence requested by Treasury to establish solvency and ability to meet obligations.

claims.quote: A certificate of authority will be effective for a term that expires on the last day of the next July. All statutory requirements and regulatory requirements under this part are continuing obligations, and any certificate issued is expressly subject to continuing compliance with such requirements. The certificate of authority will be renewed annually on the first day of August, provided that the company remains qualified under the law, the regulations in this part, and other relevant Treasury requirements, and the company submits the fee required under § 223.22 by March 1st of each year.
claims.summary: The company must remain qualified under the law, regulations, and other relevant Treasury requirements, and must submit the required fee by March 1st of each year for the renewal of the certificate of authority.

claims.quote: A company holding a certificate of authority, or its agent, may only execute (sign or otherwise validate) a surety bond in favor of the United States in a state where it is licensed to do surety business. It need not be licensed in the state or other area in which the principal resides or where the contract is to be performed. The term other area includes the District of Columbia, American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
claims.summary: A company holding a certificate of authority, or its agent, may only execute a surety bond in favor of the United States in a state where it is licensed to do surety business.

claims.quote: Every company certified under this part or recognized as an admitted reinsurer pursuant to
claims.summary: Every company certified under this part or recognized as an admitted reinsurer must notify Treasury of changes.

claims.quote: § 223.12(h) must notify Treasury of changes that have a significant impact on its financial statements or solvency during the term of such certification or admission.
claims.summary: The company must notify Treasury of changes that have a significant impact on its financial statements or solvency during the term of such certification or admission.

claims.quote: § 223.12(h) must notify Treasury of the following: (1) Capital changes. Companies must forward to Treasury, when available, approvals by the insurance authorities of the company's state regulator when changes in paid-up capital or contributions or withdrawals to surplus have occurred;
claims.summary: Companies must forward to Treasury, when available, approvals by the insurance authorities of the company's state regulator when changes in paid-up capital or contributions or withdrawals to surplus have occurred.

claims.quote: (2) Changes in stock ownership. Stock insurance companies must provide a statement signed and sworn to by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary and by the Treasurer or Assistant Treasurer of the company each time any person (whether an individual, corporation, or organization of any kind) becomes owner of more than 5 percent of any class of outstanding stock issued by the company;
claims.summary: Stock insurance companies must provide a statement signed and sworn to by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary and by the Treasurer or Assistant Treasurer of the company each time any person becomes owner of more than 5 percent of any class of outstanding stock issued by the company.

claims.quote: (3) Mergers, transfer, assumption, and group/pool restructuring. Companies must notify Treasury at least six months prior to any merger, consolidation, transfer, assumption, material group or pool restructuring, or name changes in which the reporting company is involved. The company must furnish to Treasury copies or agreements or documents pertaining to the same, as approved by the insurance authorities of the company's state regulator;
claims.summary: Companies must notify Treasury at least six months prior to any merger, consolidation, transfer, assumption, material group or pool restructuring, or name changes in which the reporting company is involved. The company must furnish to Treasury copies or agreements or documents pertaining to the same, as approved by the insurance authorities of the company's state regulator.

claims.quote: (4) Charters and bylaws amendments. Whenever a company amends its charter or bylaws it must submit a certified copy of the amended charter or bylaws to Treasury.
claims.summary: Whenever a company amends its charter or bylaws it must submit a certified copy of the amended charter or bylaws to Treasury.

claims.quote: (b) Noncompliance with this section may result in Treasury denying a company's application for its certificate of authority, its recognition as an admitted reinsurer, renewal of its certificate of authority, or renewal of its recognition as an admitted reinsurer; or in Treasury revoking a company's certificate of authority or recognition as an admitted reinsurer.
claims.summary: Noncompliance with this section may result in Treasury denying a company's application for its certificate of authority, its recognition as an admitted reinsurer, renewal of its certificate of authority, or renewal of its recognition as an admitted reinsurer; or in Treasury revoking a company's certificate of authority or recognition as an admitted reinsurer.

claims.quote: normal account balances may be evaluated for transactional substance, quality, and liquidity.
claims.summary: Normal account balances must be evaluated for transactional substance, quality, and liquidity.

claims.quote: Some assets that may be admissible under codification and/or certain state permitted practices may require supporting documentation as needed on a case-by-case basis in order to be admissible under Treasury's criteria.
claims.summary: Some assets may require supporting documentation on a case-by-case basis to be admissible under Treasury's criteria.

claims.quote: Assets resulting from reinsurance transactions must meet the credit for reinsurance standards listed under paragraph (c) of this section.
claims.summary: Assets resulting from reinsurance transactions must meet the credit for reinsurance standards listed under paragraph (c) of this section.

claims.quote: Bonds, unaffiliated common stocks, and unaffiliated preferred stocks must be valued and reported in accordance with the NAIC's Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (as updated or amended from time to time) and the NA,IC Securities Valuation Office (SVO).
claims.summary: Bonds, unaffiliated common stocks, and unaffiliated preferred stocks must be valued and reported in accordance with the NAIC's Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual and the NAIC Securities Valuation Office.

claims.quote: The value of all other securities should be valued as of December 31 and reported in U.S. Dollars.
claims.summary: The value of all other securities should be valued as of December 31 and reported in U.S. Dollars.

claims.quote: For securities that do not have a SVO designation or have a SVO non-investment grade designation and are significant for Treasury purposes, Treasury may consider, if it deems appropriate, other relevant data (e.g., prospectus, marketability/liquidity information, internal investment strategies/philosophies) and perform an analysis to determine whether the securities meet Treasury's criteria for admissibility.
claims.summary: Treasury may consider other relevant data and perform an analysis to determine whether securities meet Treasury's criteria for admissibility.

claims.quote: Investments in subsidiaries, controlled entities, and affiliated entities must be reported in accordance with the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (as updated or amended from time to time).
claims.summary: Investments in subsidiaries, controlled entities, and affiliated entities must be reported in accordance with the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual.

claims.quote: Companies owning securities of other insurance companies, which are under the same direction and control as the reporting company, must furnish copies of the NAIC File Upload of the subsidiaries. The assets of these subsidiaries will be analyzed according to the criteria set forth in this section.
claims.summary: Companies owning securities of other insurance companies must furnish copies of the NAIC File Upload of the subsidiaries and have their assets analyzed according to the criteria set forth in this section.

claims.quote: Companies owning securities of non-insurance companies, which are under the same direction and control as the reporting company, must furnish copies of independently audited financial statements of such companies as of the reporting date.
claims.summary: Companies owning securities of non-insurance companies must furnish copies of independently audited financial statements of such companies as of the reporting date.

claims.quote: Only real estate essential to the operating needs of the company for conducting its business, and conventional first mortgage loans on unencumbered, improved, or productive real estate located within the United States, are admissible.
claims.summary: Only real estate essential to the operating needs of the company and conventional first mortgage loans on real estate located within the United States are admissible.

claims.quote: These must be reported in accordance with the NAIC's Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (as updated or amended from time to time).
claims.summary: Real estate and mortgages must be reported in accordance with the NAIC's Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual.

claims.quote: The real estate and mortgaged property must be supported by an appraisal report that includes the information and computations normally used in arriving at a competent appraised value.
claims.summary: Real estate and mortgaged property must be supported by an appraisal report that includes the information and computations normally used in arriving at a competent appraised value.

claims.quote: In instances where the aggregate values exceed 20 percent of the policyholders' surplus, Treasury may, if it deems appropriate, require additional supporting documentation.
claims.summary: In instances where the aggregate values exceed 20 percent of the policyholders' surplus, Treasury may require additional supporting documentation.

claims.quote: Companies transacting surety bail business must submit a schedule showing bail premiums in force, bail liability, and the amount of any associated unearned premium reserve.
claims.summary: Companies transacting surety bail business must submit a schedule showing bail premiums in force, bail liability, and the amount of any associated unearned premium reserve.

claims.quote: Companies are required to submit Treasury Schedule F (Treasury Form No. TFS 6314) reflecting information in the company's annual statements.
claims.summary: Companies are required to submit Treasury Schedule F reflecting information in the company's annual statements.

claims.quote: Companies must maintain RBC results that fall within acceptable ranges as established by the NAIC or provide a satisfactory explanation for results that do not.
claims.summary: Companies must maintain RBC results within acceptable ranges as established by the NAIC or provide a satisfactory explanation for results that do not.

claims.quote: Companies must maintain results for these ratios that fall within acceptable ranges as established by the NAIC or provide a satisfactory explanation for results that do not.
claims.summary: Companies must maintain results for the NAIC IRIS ratios within acceptable ranges as established by the NAIC or provide a satisfactory explanation for results that do not.

claims.quote: Treasury may require companies to submit additional documentation or explanation regarding financial statements with evidence of negative financial results or trends such as decreasing policyholders' surplus, large underwriting losses, negative cashflows, or unsatisfactory IRIS ratio results.
claims.summary: Companies may be required to submit additional documentation or explanation regarding financial statements with evidence of negative financial results or trends.

claims.quote: Noncompliance with paragraphs (a) through (f) of this section may result in Treasury denying a company's application for its certificate of authority, or renewal of its certificate, or in Treasury revoking a company's certificate.
claims.summary: Noncompliance with paragraphs (a) to (f) may result in Treasury denying a company's application for its certificate of authority, renewal of its certificate, or revoking its certificate.

claims.quote: no company holding a certificate of authority shall underwrite any single risk on any bond or policy on behalf of any individual, firm, association, or corporation, whether or not the United States is interested as a party thereto, the amount of which is greater than 10 percent of the paid-up capital and surplus of such company, as determined by Treasury.
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: A company holding a certificate of authority is prohibited from underwriting any single risk on any bond or policy on behalf of any individual, firm, association, or corporation, if the amount exceeds 10 percent of the company's paid-up capital and surplus as determined by Treasury.

claims.quote: Such figure ( i.e., 10 percent of a company's paid-up capital and surplus as determined by Treasury) is hereinafter referred to as the underwriting limitation.
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: The underwriting limitation is defined as 10 percent of a company's paid-up capital and surplus as determined by Treasury.

claims.quote: In determining the underwriting limitation, the full penalty of any surety and fidelity obligation will be regarded as the liability, and no offset will be allowed on account of any estimate of risk that is less than such full penalty, except in the following cases:
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: The full penalty of any surety and fidelity obligation will be regarded as the liability when determining the underwriting limitation, with no offset allowed for any estimate of risk less than the full penalty, except in specified cases.

claims.quote: (1) Appeal bonds; in which case the liability will be regarded as the amount of the judgment appealed from, plus 10 percent of said amount to cover interest and costs;
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: For appeal bonds, the liability will be regarded as the amount of the judgment appealed from, plus 10 percent of said amount to cover interest and costs.

claims.quote: (2) Bonds of executors, administrators, trustees, guardians, and other fiduciaries, where the penalty of the bond or other obligation is fixed in excess of the estimated value of the estate; in which cases the estimated value of the estate, upon which the penalty of the bond was fixed, will be regarded as the liability;
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: For bonds of executors, administrators, trustees, guardians, and other fiduciaries where the penalty is fixed in excess of the estimated value of the estate, the estimated value of the estate will be regarded as the liability.

claims.quote: (3) Indemnifying agreements executed by sole heirs or beneficiaries of an estate releasing the surety from liability;
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: For indemnifying agreements executed by sole heirs or beneficiaries of an estate releasing the surety from liability, the liability will be regarded as the amount of the indemnifying agreement.

claims.quote: (4) Contract bonds given in excess of the amount of the contract; in which cases the amount of the contract will be regarded as the liability;
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: For contract bonds given in excess of the amount of the contract, the amount of the contract will be regarded as the liability.

claims.quote: (5) Bonds for banks or trust companies as principals, conditioned to repay moneys on deposit, whereby pursuant to any law or decree of a court, the amount to be deposited shall be less than the penalty of the bond; in which cases the maximum amount on deposit at any one time will be regarded as the liability.
claims.affected_party: company holding a certificate of authority
claims.summary: For bonds for banks or trust companies as principals, conditioned to repay moneys on deposit, where the amount to be deposited is less than the penalty of the bond, the maximum amount on deposit at any one time will be regarded as the liability.

claims.quote: Each company must limit its liability upon the face of the bond or policy to an amount which must be within its respective underwriting limitation.
claims.summary: Each company must limit its liability on the face of the bond or policy to an amount within its underwriting limitation.

claims.quote: a company writing such bonds must reinsure liability in excess of the underwriting limitation with one or more companies holding a certificate of authority from Treasury within 45 days from the date of execution and delivery of the bond.
claims.summary: A company writing bonds running to the United States must reinsure liability in excess of its underwriting limitation within 45 days.

claims.quote: Such reinsurance shall not be in excess of the underwriting limitation of the reinsuring company.
claims.summary: Reinsurance shall not exceed the underwriting limitation of the reinsuring company.

claims.quote: Within the 45-day period, the direct writing company shall furnish to the Federal agency any requested reinsurance agreements.
claims.summary: The direct writing company must furnish any requested reinsurance agreements to the Federal agency within the 45-day period.

claims.quote: the direct writing company must execute the following reinsurance agreement forms: Standard Form 273 (Reinsurance Agreement for a Bonds Statute Performance Bond), Standard Form 274 (Reinsurance Agreement for a Bonds Statute Payment Bond), and Standard Form 275 (Reinsurance Agreement in Favor of the United States).
claims.summary: The direct writing company must execute the specified reinsurance agreement forms for bonds required by the Miller Act.

claims.quote: A company holding a certificate of authority from Treasury writing risks covered by bonds or policies not running to the United States, to the extent that its excess liability is not addressed through another protective method specified in this section, must reinsure liability in excess of its underwriting limitation within 45 days from the date of execution and delivery of the bond or policy with any of: (i) One or more companies holding a certificate of authority from Treasury; (ii) One or more companies recognized as a reinsurer in accordance with § 223.12, except for any reinsurer who is required by a U.S. state to post 100 percent collateral; (iii) A pool, association, etc., to the extent that it is composed of such companies; or (iv) An instrumentality or agency of the United States that is permitted by Federal law or regulation to execute reinsurance contracts.
claims.summary: A company writing bonds or policies not running to the United States must reinsure liability in excess of its underwriting limitation within 45 days with specified entities.

claims.quote: No certificate-holding company may cede to a reinsuring company recognized under
claims.summary: No certificate-holding company may cede liability to a reinsuring company recognized under the specified regulations.

claims.quote: the excess liability may be protected: (1) By the deposit with the company in pledge, or by conveyance to it in trust for its protection, of assets admitted by Treasury, the current market value of which is at least equal to the liability in excess of its underwriting limitation.
claims.summary: The company must protect excess liability by depositing assets with it in pledge or conveying assets to it in trust for its protection.

claims.quote: Treasury may, on a case-by-case basis, consider a letter of credit provided by a financial institution to be adequate security under this paragraph (c) if Treasury can verify that the assets referenced in the letter of credit are pledged exclusively to secure the excess risk, and if the letter of credit meets other requirements Treasury might prescribe.
claims.summary: Treasury may consider a letter of credit as adequate security if it verifies that the referenced assets are pledged exclusively to secure the excess risk and the letter of credit meets other requirements.

claims.quote: Assets used to protect excess liability pursuant to this paragraph (c) cannot also be used to obtain credit for reinsurance pursuant to § 223.9(c).
claims.summary: Assets used to protect excess liability under this paragraph cannot also be used to obtain credit for reinsurance pursuant to § 223.9(c).

claims.quote: If such obligation was incurred on behalf of or on account of a fiduciary holding property in a trust capacity, by a joint control agreement providing that the whole or a sufficient portion of the property so held may not be disposed of or pledged in any way without the consent of the insuring company.
claims.summary: A joint control agreement must be in place to ensure that the whole or a sufficient portion of the property held in trust may not be disposed of or pledged without the consent of the insuring company.

claims.quote: Protect liability in excess of their underwriting limit on risks not running to the United States by reinsuring excess liability with a reinsurer recognized pursuant to this section.
claims.summary: A company must protect liability in excess of their underwriting limit on risks not running to the United States by reinsuring excess liability with a reinsurer recognized pursuant to this section.

claims.quote: Every company applying for recognition by Treasury as one of the categories of reinsurers in paragraphs (c) through (j) of this section, or annual renewal of such recognition, shall submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location, and in the manner, specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/. The applicant company must submit the documentation and must meet the requirements as outlined in this section and in supplemental guidance published by Treasury on its website.
claims.summary: Every company applying for recognition by Treasury as one of the categories of reinsurers or for annual renewal of such recognition must submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location and in the manner specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/. The applicant company must submit the documentation and meet the requirements as outlined in this section and in supplemental guidance published by Treasury on its website.

claims.quote: A company is not eligible for recognition under this section if it only insures or reinsures risks of its parent, affiliated, or controlled unaffiliated business, or is deemed by Treasury to be primarily engaged in self-insurance.
claims.summary: A company is not eligible for recognition under this section if it only insures or reinsures risks of its parent, affiliated, or controlled unaffiliated business, or is deemed by Treasury to be primarily engaged in self-insurance.

claims.quote: Noncompliance with the requirements of this section may result in a company's application for recognition, or for renewal of its recognition, being denied.
claims.summary: Noncompliance with the requirements of this section may result in a company's application for recognition, or for renewal of its recognition, being denied.

claims.summary: Any company organized under the laws of the United States or of any state thereof, wishing to apply for recognition as an admitted reinsurer of surety companies doing business with the United States, shall submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location and in the manner specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/. claims.summary: The request must indicate the reason for applying for recognition, whether the company has previously applied for recognition, whether Treasury approved the application, and the applicable dates, as well as the reason for termination of previous recognition and the applicable date.

claims.quote: A certified copy of its charter or articles of incorporation with all amendments as of the date of application showing the legal name of the company and that it is authorized to write reinsurance;
claims.summary: The company must provide a certified copy of its charter or articles of incorporation with all amendments as of the date of application, showing the legal name of the company and that it is authorized to write reinsurance.

claims.quote: A listing of the names of the company's current officers and directors as of the date of application, including a biographical affidavit of each officer and director per instructions online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/;
claims.summary: The company must provide a listing of the names of its current officers and directors as of the date of application, including a biographical affidavit of each officer and director per instructions online.

claims.quote: A certified copy of a license from any one state in which it has been authorized to do business showing its authority to write reinsurance and/or other lines of insurance;
claims.summary: The company must provide a certified copy of a license from any one state in which it has been authorized to do business, showing its authority to write reinsurance and/or other lines of insurance.

claims.quote: IRIS ratio results, and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC for the last two years preceding the date of application;
claims.summary: The company must provide IRIS ratio results and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC for the last two years preceding the date of application.

claims.quote: A memorandum setting forth the company's method of operation, including lines of business written, the company's underwriting and claims philosophy, and significant changes in the company's operations or corporate structure that impact its financial statements;
claims.summary: The company must provide a memorandum setting forth its method of operation, including lines of business written, the company's underwriting and claims philosophy, and significant changes in its operations or corporate structure that impact its financial statements.

claims.quote: A completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in § 223.9(c) for two years preceding the date of application;
claims.summary: The company must provide a completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in § 223.9(c), for two years preceding the date of application.

claims.quote: A Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the last two years preceding the date of application provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC;
claims.summary: The company must provide a Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the last two years preceding the date of application, provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves, with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC.

claims.quote: Such other evidence as Treasury may request to establish that the company is solvent and able to meet the continuing obligation to carry out its contracts.
claims.summary: The company must provide such other evidence as Treasury may request to establish that the company is solvent and able to meet the continuing obligation to carry out its contracts.

claims.quote: The submissions listed in paragraphs (h)(1)(i) through (xii) of this section, except that the financial statement of such branch shall show that it has net assets of not less than $250,000 over and above all liabilities; and (ii) Evidence satisfactory to Treasury to establish that it has on deposit in the United States not less than $25,000 available to its policyholders and creditors in the United States.
claims.summary: The applicant must submit the listed submissions and provide evidence satisfactory to Treasury to establish that it has on deposit in the United States not less than $250,000 available to its policyholders and creditors in the United States.

claims.quote: Any company recognized pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) or (2) of this section wishing to apply for renewal of its recognition shall submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location, and in the manner, specified online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/.
claims.summary: A company recognized pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) or (2) of this section wishing to apply for renewal of its recognition must submit an application to Treasury, c/o Surety Bonds Program, to the location and in the manner specified online.

claims.quote: The company must file the following data with Treasury and shall transmit therewith the fee in accordance with the provisions of
claims.summary: The company must file the following data with Treasury and transmit therewith the fee in accordance with the provisions.

claims.quote: Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of
claims.summary: The applicant must pay the application fee in accordance with the provisions.

claims.quote: A copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department including a copy of company responses to any significant findings or recommendations;
claims.summary: The company must submit a copy of the latest available report of its examination by its domiciliary State Insurance Department, including a copy of company responses to any significant findings or recommendations.

claims.quote: Annual statements of its financial condition, as of the close of the preceding year, on the annual statement form of the NAIC with all Schedules and Exhibits completed, including copies of the NAIC File Upload, showing that it has paid-up capital of at least $250,000 in cash or its equivalent, in the case of a stock insurance company, or has net assets of not less than $500,000 over and above all liabilities, in the case of a mutual insurance company.
claims.summary: The company must submit annual statements of its financial condition, as of the close of the preceding year, on the annual statement form of the NAIC with all Schedules and Exhibits completed, including copies of the NAIC File Upload, showing that it has paid-up capital of at least $250,000 in cash or its equivalent, or has net assets of not less than $500,000 over and above all liabilities.

claims.quote: The Annual Financial Statement's Jurat Page (only) is to be signed (facsimile signatures are acceptable) by the company President, Secretary, and a Notary Public who shall also affix a notary seal;
claims.summary: The Annual Financial Statement's Jurat Page (only) must be signed by the company President, Secretary, and a Notary Public who shall also affix a notary seal.

claims.quote: IRIS ratio results, and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC as of the close of the preceding year;
claims.summary: The company must submit IRIS ratio results and an explanation for any ratios outside the normal ranges as established by the NAIC as of the close of the preceding year.

claims.quote: A completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in
claims.summary: The company must submit a completed Treasury Schedule F (Form No. TFS 6314), as referenced in the document.

claims.quote: A Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the preceding year provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC;
claims.summary: The company must submit a Statement of Actuarial Opinion as of the close of the preceding year provided by a qualified actuary, as defined by the NAIC, on the adequacy of all loss reserves, with the scope and format of the statement also conforming to the requirements of the NAIC.

claims.quote: A listing of the names of the company's current officers and directors as of the close of the preceding year, including a biographical affidavit of each new officer and director per instructions online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/surety-bonds/;
claims.summary: The company must submit a listing of the names of its current officers and directors as of the close of the preceding year, including a biographical affidavit of each new officer and director per instructions online.

claims.quote: To obtain recognition as a complementary reinsurer, the company must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions of
claims.summary: To obtain recognition as a complementary reinsurer, the company must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions.

claims.quote: Meet and maintain all capital and surplus, solvency, and market conduct requirements under the applicable Covered Agreement;
claims.summary: Must meet and maintain all capital and surplus, solvency, and market conduct requirements under the applicable Covered Agreement.

claims.quote: Be recognized by at least one U.S. state as a Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer, as defined by the state's credit for reinsurance law or regulation based on the NAIC's Credit for Reinsurance Model Law and Regulation, and submit proof of such recognition;
claims.summary: Must be recognized by at least one U.S. state as a Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer and submit proof of such recognition.

claims.quote: Any company may apply for recognition or annual renewal of such recognition as an alien reinsurer, provided it is licensed to write reinsurance by, and has its head office or domicile in, a non-U.S. jurisdiction that is recognized by a U.S. state as a Qualified Jurisdiction or as a Reciprocal Jurisdiction, provided that the Reciprocal Jurisdiction is not party to an in-force Covered Agreement as described in paragraph (i) of this section.
claims.summary: May apply for recognition or annual renewal of such recognition as an alien reinsurer, provided it is licensed to write reinsurance by, and has its head office or domicile in, a non-U.S. jurisdiction that is recognized by a U.S. state as a Qualified Jurisdiction or as a Reciprocal Jurisdiction, provided that the Reciprocal Jurisdiction is not party to an in-force Covered Agreement as described in paragraph (i) of this section.

claims.quote: To obtain such recognition, the company must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22
claims.summary: Must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.

claims.quote: Be recognized by at least one U.S. state as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or a “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer,” as defined by the state's credit for reinsurance law or regulation based on the NAIC's Credit for Reinsurance Model Law and Regulation, and submit proof of such recognition;
claims.summary: Must be recognized by at least one U.S. state as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or a “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer,” and submit proof of such recognition.

claims.quote: Meet and maintain all capital and surplus, market conduct, and other requirements for eligibility as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer” in accordance with the law and regulation of all U.S. states granting it such recognition;
claims.summary: Must meet and maintain all capital and surplus, market conduct, and other requirements for eligibility as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer” in accordance with the law and regulation of all U.S. states granting it such recognition.

claims.quote: Submit to Treasury: (i) For initial applications for recognition, all information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the two most recently completed calendar years. (ii) For applications for renewal of such recognition, all annual filing information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the most recently completed calendar year. (iii) Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.
claims.summary: Must submit to Treasury: (i) For initial applications for recognition, all information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the two most recently completed calendar years. (ii) For applications for renewal of such recognition, all annual filing information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the most recently completed calendar year. (iii) Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.

claims.quote: Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.
claims.summary: Must pay the application fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.

claims.quote: Treasury determines the amount of paid-up capital and surplus of any company holding or seeking a certificate of authority or recognized (or seeking recognition) as an admitted reinsurer pursuant to § 223.12(h) on an insurance accounting basis under the regulations in this part, from the company's financial statements and other information, or by such examination of the company at its own expense as Treasury may deem appropriate.
claims.summary: Treasury determines the amount of paid-up capital and surplus of any company holding or seeking a certificate of authority or recognized (or seeking recognition) as an admitted reinsurer pursuant to § 223.12(h) on an insurance accounting basis under the regulations in this part, from the company's financial statements and other information, or by such examination of the company at its own expense as Treasury may deem appropriate.

claims.quote: A list of certificate holding companies is published annually as of August 1 in Department Circular No. 570, Companies Holding Certificates of Authority as Acceptable Sureties on Federal Bonds and as Acceptable Reinsuring Companies, with information as to underwriting limitations, areas in which listed sureties are licensed to transact surety business, and other details.
claims.summary: A list of certificate holding companies must be published annually as of August 1 in Department Circular No. 570.

claims.quote: If Treasury shall take any exceptions to the financial statements submitted by a company or other information pertinent to the company's financial solvency, before issuing Department Circular 570, Treasury shall give a company due notice of such exceptions.
claims.summary: Treasury must give a company due notice of any exceptions to the financial statements or other information pertinent to the company's financial solvency before issuing Department Circular 570.

claims.quote: A bond underwritten by a certified company on the Department Circular No. 570 list may be presented to an agency bond-approving official for acceptance.
claims.affected_party: principal required to furnish the bond
claims.summary: A bond underwritten by a certified company on the Department Circular No. 570 list may be presented to an agency bond-approving official for acceptance.

claims.quote: Selection of a particular qualified company from among all companies holding certificates of authority is discretionary with the principal required to furnish the bond, but the acceptance of a bond by an agency bond-approving official is subject to
claims.summary: The acceptance of a bond by an agency bond-approving official is subject to certain conditions, though the selection of a qualified company is discretionary with the principal required to furnish the bond.

claims.quote: An agency bond-approving official may decline to accept bonds underwritten by a certified company for cause, but only if the company has been given advance written notice by such agency.
claims.summary: An agency bond-approving official may decline to accept bonds underwritten by a certified company for cause, but only if the company has been given advance written notice.

claims.quote: The advance written notice shall: (i) State the intention of the agency to decline bonds underwritten by the company; (ii) State the reasons for or cause of the proposed declination of such bonds; (iii) Provide the company with an opportunity to rebut the stated reasons or cause; and (iv) Provide the company with an opportunity to cure the stated reasons or cause.
claims.summary: The advance written notice shall state the intention of the agency to decline bonds underwritten by the company, state the reasons for or cause of the proposed declination, provide the company with an opportunity to rebut the stated reasons or cause, and provide the company with an opportunity to cure the stated reasons or cause.

claims.quote: The agency may decline to accept bonds underwritten by the company if, after consideration of any submission by the company or failure of the company to respond to the agency's notice, the agency issues a written determination that the bonds should not be accepted, consistent with agency authorities.
claims.summary: The agency may decline to accept bonds underwritten by the company if, after consideration of any submission by the company or failure of the company to respond to the agency's notice, the agency issues a written determination that the bonds should not be accepted, consistent with agency authorities.

claims.quote: The agency shall articulate its procedures and for cause standards for declining to accept bonds in an agency regulation prior to declining any bonds in specific cases. The agency regulation should be subject to notice and comment rulemaking.
claims.summary: The agency shall articulate its procedures and for cause standards for declining to accept bonds in an agency regulation prior to declining any bonds in specific cases. The agency regulation should be subject to notice and comment rulemaking.

claims.quote: For cause includes, but is not limited to, circumstances when a surety has not paid or satisfied an administratively final bond obligation due the agency.
claims.summary: For cause includes, but is not limited to, circumstances when a surety has not paid or satisfied an administratively final bond obligation due the agency.

claims.quote: The agency regulation should define when a bond obligation becomes administratively final under the agency's procedures.
claims.summary: The agency regulation should define when a bond obligation becomes administratively final under the agency's procedures.

claims.quote: Agencies that decline bonds under this section are encouraged to use best efforts to ensure that persons conducting business with the agency are aware that bonds underwritten by the particular certified company will not be accepted.
claims.summary: Agencies that decline bonds under this section are encouraged to use best efforts to ensure that persons conducting business with the agency are aware that bonds underwritten by the particular certified company will not be accepted.

claims.quote: The agency's authority to decline bonds under this section does not apply: (i) When the underlying obligation or other for cause reason that forms the basis for the agency's written determination to decline bonds under paragraph (b)(2) of this section, or the agency written determination to decline bonds, has been stayed or enjoined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or (ii) To otherwise acceptable payment and performance contract bonds, when the agency has already accepted a project bid bond on a contract before making the written determination under paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
claims.summary: The agency's authority to decline bonds under this section does not apply when the underlying obligation or other for cause reason that forms the basis for the agency's written determination to decline bonds has been stayed or enjoined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or to otherwise acceptable payment and performance contract bonds when the agency has already accepted a project bid bond on a contract before making the written determination.

claims.quote: Notwithstanding any provision of this section, an agency bond-approving official may decline a bond from a Treasury-certified surety without advance notice if the bond is not executed in proper form, or is not in the correct penal sum amount, or is otherwise technically deficient on its face.
claims.summary: An agency bond-approving official may decline a bond from a Treasury-certified surety without advance notice if the bond is not executed in proper form, or is not in the correct penal sum amount, or is otherwise technically deficient on its face.

claims.quote: A revocation of a company's certificate of authority under § 223.19 or § 223.20 precludes the company from underwriting or reinsuring additional bonds for any agency, and therefore revokes the company's opportunity to have its bonds presented to any agency bond-approving official for acceptance.
claims.summary: A revocation of a company's certificate of authority under § 223.19 or § 223.20 precludes the company from underwriting or reinsuring additional bonds for any agency, and therefore revokes the company's opportunity to have its bonds presented to any agency bond-approving official for acceptance.

claims.quote: Whenever Treasury has reason to believe that a company is not complying with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 9304-9308 and/or the regulations under this part, including but not limited to a failure to satisfy corporate and financial standards, Treasury shall: (a) Notify the company of the facts or conduct which indicate such non-compliance, and provide the company an opportunity to respond, and (b) Revoke a company's certificate of authority after providing notice to the company if: (1) The company does not respond satisfactorily to Treasury's notification of non-compliance, or (2) The company responded, was provided an opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance, and failed to do so.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify the company of non-compliance and provide an opportunity to respond. Treasury must revoke the company's certificate of authority if the company fails to respond satisfactorily or fails to demonstrate compliance.

claims.quote: The agency shall certify that: (1) The bond obligations that are the subject of the complaint are administratively final under the agency's regulations or other authorities; (2) The company has not paid or satisfied those bond obligations; and (3) The company's obligation to pay or satisfy the bond obligations has not been stayed or enjoined by a court of competent jurisdiction.
claims.summary: The agency must certify that the bond obligations are administratively final, the company has not paid or satisfied the obligations, and the obligation has not been stayed or enjoined by a court.

claims.quote: The agency shall include in its complaint copies of the bonds, and documentation indicating that, for each such bond provided: (1) The agency has determined, consistent with agency authorities, the principal is in default on the obligation covered by the bond. Alternatively, if the default has been litigated, documentation indicating a court of competent jurisdiction has determined the principal is in default; (2) The agency made a written demand with the company on the bond requesting payment or satisfaction on its own behalf, consistent with agency authorities, or on behalf of laborers, materialmen, or suppliers (on payment bonds), based on the default status of the principal; (3) The agency afforded the company the opportunity to request administrative review within the agency contesting the agency's demand on the bond; (4) The agency made a final administrative determination that the bond obligation was due after the completion of such administrative review, or after the time period for the company to request administrative review within the agency has expired; (5) The agency provided the company the opportunity to enter into a written agreement to pay or satisfy the bond; and (6) The company has not made full payment or fully satisfied the demand, and the claim on the bond is past due.
claims.summary: The agency must include copies of the bonds and documentation indicating that the principal is in default, the agency made a written demand, afforded the company an opportunity for administrative review, made a final determination that the obligation is due, provided the company an opportunity to enter into a written agreement, and that the company has not made full payment or satisfied the demand.

claims.quote: On receipt of a complaint meeting the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, Treasury will notify the company of the agency complaint. The notice will require the company to submit a written explanatory response to Treasury within 20 business days of the date of the notice. The notice will advise the company of the facts and conduct referenced in the complaint. Treasury will attach a copy of the incoming complaint to the notice. The notice will afford the company the opportunity to address the complaint and demonstrate its qualifications to retain its certificate of authority.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify the company of the agency complaint, require the company to submit a written response within 20 business days, advise the company of the facts and conduct referenced in the complaint, attach a copy of the incoming complaint, and afford the company the opportunity to address the complaint and demonstrate its qualifications.

claims.quote: The designated Treasury official (with executive oversight over the Treasury surety program, at the Assistant Commissioner level or equivalent) will appoint a Treasury Reviewing Official to conduct a review of the agency complaint referenced in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, and the company response referenced in paragraph (c) of this section, to determine whether revocation of the company's certificate of authority is warranted.
claims.summary: The designated Treasury official must appoint a Treasury Reviewing Official to conduct a review of the agency complaint and company response to determine if revocation of the company's certificate of authority is warranted.

claims.quote: The Reviewing Official is authorized to require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official is authorized to require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company.

claims.quote: Upon completion of such review, the Reviewing Official shall prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the designated Treasury official setting forth findings and a recommended disposition.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official must prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the designated Treasury official setting forth findings and a recommended disposition.

claims.quote: The designated Treasury official will be the Deciding Official who will make the final decision whether the company's certificate of authority to write and reinsure bonds should be revoked based on the administrative record.
claims.summary: The designated Treasury official must be the Deciding Official who will make the final decision whether the company's certificate of authority to write and reinsure bonds should be revoked based on the administrative record.

claims.quote: If the Deciding Official's final decision is that revocation is not warranted, the company and the agency will be notified of the basis of this decision and the complaint against the company will be dismissed.
claims.summary: If the Deciding Official's final decision is that revocation is not warranted, the company and the agency must be notified of the basis of this decision and the complaint against the company will be dismissed.

claims.quote: If the Deciding Official's final decision is that the company's certificate of authority shall be revoked, the Deciding Official will notify the company and the agency of the revocation decision and the basis for such decision.
claims.summary: If the Deciding Official's final decision is that the company's certificate of authority shall be revoked, the Deciding Official must notify the company and the agency of the revocation decision and the basis for such decision.

claims.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (g) of this section, the notice will afford the company an opportunity to cure its noncompliance by paying or satisfying the bonds (including payment of any interest, penalties, and fees) forming the basis of the final decision within 20 business days.
claims.summary: The company must have an opportunity to cure its noncompliance by paying or satisfying the bonds (including payment of any interest, penalties, and fees) forming the basis of the final decision within 20 business days.

claims.quote: If the company cures its noncompliance within 20 business days, the complaint against the company will be deemed moot and the company will retain its certificate of authority to write Federal bonds.
claims.summary: If the company cures its noncompliance within 20 business days, the complaint against the company will be deemed moot and the company will retain its certificate of authority to write Federal bonds.

claims.quote: If the company does not cure its noncompliance within 20 business days, the company's certificate of authority shall be revoked by Treasury without further notice.
claims.summary: If the company does not cure its noncompliance within 20 business days, the company's certificate of authority shall be revoked by Treasury without further notice.

claims.quote: In reviewing whether the revocation of the company's certificate of authority is warranted under this section, the Reviewing Official will recommend, and the Deciding Official will determine, whether the default is clear and whether the company's failure to pay or satisfy the bonds is based on inadequate grounds.
claims.summary: In reviewing whether the revocation of the company's certificate of authority is warranted under this section, the Reviewing Official must recommend, and the Deciding Official must determine, whether the default is clear and whether the company's failure to pay or satisfy the bonds is based on inadequate grounds.

claims.quote: The company is not entitled to an opportunity to cure its noncompliance if its conduct in failing to carry out its contracts is willful.
claims.summary: The company is not entitled to an opportunity to cure its noncompliance if its conduct in failing to carry out its contracts is willful.

claims.quote: For purposes of this regulation, “willful” means a careless or reckless disregard of a known legal obligation to satisfy an administratively final bond obligation.
claims.summary: For purposes of this regulation, 'willful' means a careless or reckless disregard of a known legal obligation to satisfy an administratively final bond obligation.

claims.quote: If a company that is the subject of a complaint under paragraph (a) and (b) of this section believes the opportunity to make known its views, as provided for under paragraph (c) of this section, is inadequate, it may, within 20 business days of the date of the notice required by paragraph (c), request, in writing, that an informal hearing be convened.
claims.summary: A company may request an informal hearing within 20 business days if it believes its opportunity to present its views is inadequate.

claims.quote: As soon as possible after a written request for an informal hearing is received, the Reviewing Official shall convene an informal hearing, at such time and place as he or she deems appropriate, for the purpose of determining whether the company's certificate of authority should be revoked.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official must convene an informal hearing as soon as possible after receiving a written request.

claims.quote: The company shall be advised, in writing, of the time and place of the informal hearing and shall be directed to bring all documents, records and other information as it may find necessary and relevant to support its position.
claims.summary: The company must be advised in writing of the time and place of the informal hearing and must bring relevant documents and information.

claims.quote: The company may be represented by counsel and shall have a fair opportunity to present any relevant material and to examine the administrative record.
claims.summary: The company has the right to be represented by counsel and to present and examine relevant material and the administrative record.

claims.quote: The complaining agency may be requested by the Reviewing Official to send a representative to the hearing to present any relevant material, and the agency representative may examine the administrative record.
claims.summary: The complaining agency may be requested to send a representative to the hearing to present relevant material and examine the administrative record.

claims.quote: The Reviewing Official is authorized to require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company to ensure appropriate consideration of relevant factual or legal issues.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official may require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company to ensure appropriate consideration of relevant issues.

claims.quote: Upon completion of the informal hearing, the Review, the Reviewing Official shall prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the Deciding Official setting forth findings and a recommended disposition.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official must prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the Deciding Official upon completion of the informal hearing.

claims.quote: The administrative record consists of the Federal agency complaint referenced in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, the company response referenced in paragraph (c), any other documentation submitted to, considered by, or entered into the administrative record by the Reviewing Official, the hearing transcript, and the Reviewing Official's Recommendation Memorandum.
claims.summary: The administrative record includes the Federal agency complaint, company response, other documentation submitted, the hearing transcript, and the Reviewing Official's Recommendation Memorandum.

claims.quote: If, after one year from the date that Treasury notifies the company of its decision to decline to renew or revoke the certificate of authority of a company under this part, the company can demonstrate that the basis for the non-renewal or revocation has been cured, as determined by Treasury in its discretion, and that it can comply with, and does meet, all continuing requirements for certification under 31.U.S.C. 9304-9308 and this part, the company may submit an application to Treasury for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority, which will be granted without prejudice if all such requirements are met.
claims.summary: A company may submit an application for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority if it can demonstrate that the basis for non-renewal or revocation has been cured and it meets all continuing requirements.

claims.quote: Treasury may waive the one year waiting period for good cause shown, as determined by Treasury in its sole discretion.
claims.summary: Treasury may waive the one-year waiting period for reinstatement if good cause is shown.

claims.quote: Fees shall be imposed and collected, for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section that are performed by Treasury, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.
claims.summary: Fees must be imposed and collected for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section that are performed by Treasury, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.

claims.quote: In a given year a uniform fee will be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service, e.g., determination of a company's continuing qualifications for annual renewal of its certificate of authority.
claims.affected_party: companies requesting a particular category of service
claims.summary: A uniform fee must be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service in a given year.

claims.quote: Fees are determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.
claims.summary: Fees must be determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.

claims.quote: Specific fee information may be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program, or online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/surety-bonds/user-fees.pdf.
claims.summary: Specific fee information must be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program or online at the provided URL.

claims.quote: A notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section will be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.
claims.summary: A notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section must be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.
